text: We evaluated a learned noisy-channel model of weak-label errors refined by expectation-maximization on the sciq testbed, across 5 seeds. The method achieved a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.4. No baseline PGR was supplied in the provided data, so this number cannot be positioned as an improvement over, or a regression from, any reference method; it should be read only as the absolute level of gap recovery attained by this configuration. Likewise, no standard error or per-seed spread was reported alongside the aggregate, so the seed-to-seed variability of the 0.4 figure is unknown and we cannot characterize how tightly the estimate is bounded. A single testbed and a single method variant were examined, which limits what can be said about generality across datasets or about which component of the approach — the noisy-channel error model or the expectation-maximization refinement — drives the observed value. Further runs with a matched baseline and reported variance would be needed to interpret this result.
